input: Start a monthly family letter for distant relatives

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing what content is included — life updates, photos, stories, milestones — determines how much time and effort each edition requires and shapes the template structure.
The size and diversity of the recipient list (e.g., grandparents only vs. all extended family across generations) affects the tone, detail level, and distribution method.
Whether this is written by one person or as a collaborative family effort changes the workflow and coordination needed each month.
Whether the letter is sent physically by post or digitally by email/PDF determines the tools, cost, and production process entirely.
The desired tone — warm and personal vs. newsy and informative — shapes the writing style, length, and whether photos or design elements are included.
How much time the writer can realistically spend on each edition determines the complexity of the format and whether a simple template is essential.
Knowing what a successful letter looks like — relatives feeling connected, a consistent archive, high open/response rates — clarifies what to prioritise in the design of the letter.

gold.taskTitle: Launch a monthly family letter for relatives
gold.taskDescription: Create and send a recurring monthly letter to keep distant family members updated on family life and news.

questions.title: What content will each letter regularly cover?
questions.description: Identify the recurring sections or topics — e.g., family milestones, children's updates, travel, photos, a personal note — to define the template structure.

questions.title: Who exactly will receive the letter each month?
questions.description: Define the recipient group — grandparents only, all extended family, family friends — including an approximate number and age range, to calibrate tone and distribution.

questions.title: Will one person write it or multiple family members contribute?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a solo effort or a collaborative one, which affects the editing workflow and how contributions are gathered each month.

questions.title: Will it be sent by post, email, or another format?
questions.description: Decide the delivery method — printed and mailed, emailed as a PDF, a newsletter platform — as this drives tool choice, cost, and design requirements.

questions.title: What tone and style should the letter have?
questions.description: Clarify whether the letter should feel like a warm personal note, a designed family newsletter, a casual update, or something else — guiding writing style and visual choices.

questions.title: How much time can you spend on each monthly edition?
questions.description: Establish a realistic time budget per issue — 30 minutes vs. a few hours — to determine how simple or elaborate the format should be.

questions.title: What would make this letter feel like a success to you?
questions.description: Identify the main goal — relatives feeling more connected, preserving family memories, sparking replies — so the format and content can be designed around that outcome.
